jobs.description: Welcome to Rhenus!The Rhenus Group is one of the leading global logistics service providers. The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Every year, 225.000 patients are treated in 30 clinics, 27 institutes and specialized centers. The over 8.000 employees offer medical care with state-of-the-art diagnosis and therapies, which meet highest international standards. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral antivity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.At the Insitute of Medical Microbiology (working group of PD Dr. Torben Knuschke), we are therefore offering the following position, which is fully funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and will start on 1 January 2027Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) funtions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cellsApply molecular biology techniquesPlan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studiesPresent research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publicationsAssist in supervising Bachelors/Masters studentsA completed Master´s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related fieldSolid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniquesExperience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantageStrong interest in basic research in Virology/ImmunologyIndependent, structured, and team-oriented working-styleExcellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredAn exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research fieldDedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminarsState-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital EssenInterdisciplinary work with colleagues from other departmentsEnrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Sciences BIOME (https://www.uni-due.de/biome)Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 yearsA collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideasFamily-friendly corporate culture
